- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 2–5% of recent 7-day average.
- After a sharp spike in true price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–15% in next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is below 75% of recent 18-day moving average, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and model is over-forecasting, apply downward correction: subtract 3–8% of forecast value, especially if true outcome shows downward momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility — increase forecast by 5–10% in final 7–10 days if sentiment is bullish or event-driven.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.7 → -0.3 → +0.7), model may misread momentum — apply lag correction: delay peak forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment shifts sharply.
